sections.h2: Which Jessamine County office does what with property tax?
sections.html:
The county splits the work in two. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) puts a value on each parcel, and the sheriff sends the bills and banks the payments.

The PVA's own duties page lists what the office will not do: set rates, mail bills or take a payment. What it does is value property at full fair cash value on January 1, log deed transfers, update parcel maps and handle exemptions. The sheriff's office at 201 North Main Street in Nicholasville, staffed weekdays from 8 to 4, collects the state, county, school and district levies on real and tangible property and hands each share to the right body.

Call the PVA when your value looks wrong. Call the sheriff at (859) 885-4139 when you need a payoff or a receipt.

sections.h2: How fast has the Jessamine County tax roll grown?
sections.html:
The assessment roll has grown every year since 2013, and the 2026 total of about $6.71 billion is up 9.00 percent. Residential property is the biggest piece at roughly $5.22 billion, commercial adds about $1.04 billion and agricultural about $444 million.

Residential value alone climbed from about $3.65 billion in 2022 to $5.22 billion in 2026. A house bought a few years back can therefore carry a far larger assessment today, and each property class is reassessed on a four-year cycle, so a single bump may bundle several years of price movement.

sections.h2: How does the PVA sort Jessamine County property?
sections.html:
Four classes cover everything taxable. Where a house falls depends on its location and its acreage.

  • Residential: homes inside Nicholasville or Wilmore, whether single-family, duplex, townhouse or an empty lot.
  • County Residential: homes or land outside those cities on under 10 acres, sometimes with trailers, barns or sheds.
  • Farms: tracts of 10 acres or more, where agricultural value is set.
  • Commercial and Industrial: businesses on commercial or industrial ground, plus golf courses, apartments and trailer park land.

A farm owner who wants use-value pricing files by March 1 of the year in question, and horticultural land qualifies from 5 acres. The PVA describes the program as a way to keep farms operating and preserve farmland through tax relief.

sections.h2: When does a Jessamine County tax bill come due?
sections.html:
Bills reach the sheriff by September 15. Pay by November 1 and the bill drops 2 percent under KRS 134.020, then it sits at face value through December. January adds 5 percent, and from February the add-ons are 10 percent plus a 10 percent sheriff's fee.

After the close of business on April 15, whatever is left moves to the county clerk as a certificate of delinquency, secured by a lien on the parcel. The state revenue department describes monthly interest of 1 percent and attorney and clerk commissions from there, with a summer sale where an outside investor can purchase the bill. The clerk's website carries a delinquent tax search.

Check dates with the sheriff each fall, since Kentucky permits a delayed schedule in some counties.

sections.h2: What is the path for contesting a Jessamine County value?
sections.html:
First comes a talk with the PVA. Assessment notices usually go out in April, and the roll opens for inspection on the first Monday of May for 13 days, Saturdays included. The PVA office takes conferences by phone or in person at (859) 885-4931, and the notice and the Jessamine Journal carry the dates.

Bring something that backs a lower figure: an appraisal, photos, an insurance declaration, active listings or nearby sales.

  • Conference with the PVA during the open window.
  • If it fails, an appeal form goes to the County Clerk within one workday after the window closes, and a three-member Board of Assessment Appeals hears the case.
  • The last stop is the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, whose members the Governor appoints.

Revenue officials add that the local board meets 25 to 35 days after inspection ends and turns away appeals that lack evidence. Because every step falls in spring, fall bills cannot be contested this way.

sections.h2: Which relief programs help a Jessamine County owner?
sections.html:
Owners 65 and over, and owners ruled totally disabled, can deduct a fixed sum from assessed value. The PVA's announcement for 2025 to 2026 lists that sum as $49,100.

One exemption per household is the cap. The age exemption stays on the books while the first applicant owns and occupies the home, and it leaves with them at a sale. The disability version needs a fresh application every year, per the PVA. File at the PVA office or mail P.O. Box 530, Nicholasville, KY 40340, marked "Homestead Exemption" or "Disability Exemption", with a driver's license or birth certificate copy and, for disability, a Social Security award letter or similar proof.

Churches and charities use Revenue Form 62A023. Owners of business equipment file tangible personal property returns by May 15, and late returns draw 10 percent or 20 percent penalties.

sections.h2: What tax steps should a Jessamine County seller take before listing?
sections.html:
Start by asking the sheriff for a payoff on the current bill. The name on a September bill can still be the prior owner's, so agree on the split with the buyer in writing.

Then look the address up in the clerk's delinquent search for older years. If you hold the age exemption, tell the PVA about the sale so it can move to your next home.

Census numbers show why buyers keep arriving: 57,147 people in the July 2025 estimate, up 7.8 percent from 2020, with 22,061 housing units, a $268,100 median home value for 2020 to 2024 and two thirds of homes owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Does the PVA mail the Jessamine County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The PVA only sets assessed value. The sheriff mails and collects the bill, and the PVA's duties page says its office sets no rates and collects nothing.

faqs.q: What is the discount deadline in Jessamine County?
faqs.a: November 1. KRS 134.020 gives 2 percent off for payment on or before that date, and the face amount is due through December 31.

faqs.q: Where does an unpaid Jessamine County bill end up?
faqs.a: With the county clerk after April 15, as a certificate of delinquency with a recorded lien and interest of 1 percent per month.

faqs.q: What does the Jessamine County age 65 exemption deduct?
faqs.a: The PVA lists $49,100 for 2025 to 2026. It applies to owners who live in the home, and the state adjusts the amount every two years.

faqs.q: Can I contest my Jessamine County value in the fall?
faqs.a: Not through the standard process. The PVA conference and the clerk filing both take place in May, before bills are delivered.
